title.narrative: Emergency Shelter support for communities on St Martin's Island

description.narrative: The project will provide emergency shelter assistance to the households severely affected by cyclone Mocha, which hit the coastal areas along the Bangladesh-Myanmar border on 14th May 2023. The Cyclone caused damage to around 13,000 houses and 10,692 shelters were damaged or destroyed, with over 429,337 individuals affected. Around ten thousand Rohingya refugee households in Cox’s Bazar have been affected by the cyclone, and over 1,000 displaced. 7,757 people in St Martin are affected, with over 1,033 houses damaged or destroyed and over 250 latrines and water tubes were fully damaged. In addition, 450 livestock and and over 1000 poultry have died, and over 5000 various types of trees have been uprooted. While various actors have responded in other areas addressing basic needs, food and WASH, St Martin's Island remains in urgent need of shelter and basic food, WASH and sanitation support. This project will provide 900 people within 200 HHs in Saint Martin's with the construction of community-led shelters. It will also facilitate training and advocacy on disaster resilient housing techniques among staff and the government district/ union level of St Martin's.
